strengthProgram.why: Heavy strength and plyometric training improve running economy in distance runners without hurting endurance (Balsalobre-Fernandez 2016 meta-analysis; Blagrove 2018 review). Munich's block had 2 sessions in total.
strengthProgram.equipment: At home: a backpack you can load with books or water bottles (10-20 kg), a stair or sturdy step, a mat. Adjustable dumbbells or a kettlebell make it easier to keep loads heavy as you get stronger.
strengthProgram.placement: S1 (heavy) after the week's first quality run, so easy days stay easy; S2 (plyo + core) on a later easy or quality day, never the day before a quality run or the long run. Recovery weeks: S1 only at 2 sets. Taper week 2: one light session. Race week: none.

phases.S1: HOME STRENGTH S1, foundation (~35 min, after the run): Bulgarian split squat 3x10/leg, single-leg Romanian deadlift 3x10/leg, single-leg calf raise off a step 3x12/leg straight knee + 2x12 bent knee, single-leg glute bridge 3x12/leg, side plank 3x30 s/side. phases.S2: HOME STRENGTH S2, plyo + core (~25 min): pogo hops 3x15, skipping for height 3x20 m, step/low-box jumps 3x6, dead bug 3x10, knee Copenhagen plank 3x20 s/side. ~60 foot contacts.

phases.name: Max strength
phases.S1: HOME STRENGTH S1, max strength (~40 min, after the run): Bulgarian split squat 4x5-6/leg, single-leg Romanian deadlift 4x6/leg, single-leg calf raise 4x6-8/leg straight knee + 3x8 bent knee, single-leg hip thrust 3x8/leg, Copenhagen plank 3x20-30 s/side. Load (backpack or dumbbells) so the last rep is hard but clean; 3 s lowering, 2 min rest; add load when every set hits the top of the range.
phases.S2: HOME STRENGTH S2, plyo + core (~30 min): pogo hops 4x20, alternate-leg bounds 4x6/leg, split-squat jumps 3x6/leg, lateral line hops 3x10, dead bug 3x12, side plank 3x45 s/side. ~100 contacts, full recovery between sets.

phases.name: Maintain
phases.S1: HOME STRENGTH S1, maintain (~30 min, after the run): Bulgarian split squat 3x4-5/leg heavy, single-leg Romanian deadlift 3x5/leg, single-leg calf raise 3x6/leg heavy. Lower slowly, lift fast; 3 min rest.
phases.S2: HOME STRENGTH S2, short plyo (~20 min): pogo hops 3x20, alternate-leg bounds 3x6/leg, side plank 2x45 s/side. ~60 contacts, quality over quantity.

phases.name: Taper
phases.S1: HOME STRENGTH, taper (~20 min): split squat 2x5/leg and single-leg calf raise 2x8/leg at moderate load, pogo hops 2x15. Last strength session before Rome.

strengthProgram.recoveryWeeks: HOME STRENGTH, recovery week (~25 min): S1 exercises at 2 sets each, same load as last week. No plyometrics.

swimming.rule: An easy pool session replaces the Monday recovery run in 17 weeks; its km are spread over the week's other easy runs, so weekly running totals don't change. Recovery runs cap at 10 km and easy runs at 14 km; where that wasn't enough, a rest day became a short recovery run.
swimming.session: Easy pool session, 30-40 min (~1.5-2 km): relaxed freestyle with a few technique drills, RPE 3, no hard sets. Replaces this day's recovery run; those km moved into the week's other easy runs.

fuelTest.why: Munich: ~60% honey mix caused upper and lower GI distress all race. Find the best-tolerated race fuel before the specific block.
fuelTest.design: 4 strategies x 2 long runs each, counterbalanced A-B-C-D-D-C-B-A so the rising carb target (40 -> 65 g/h) affects all equally.

strategies.D: honey only, ~24% (same dilution as B; isolates fructose ratio)

fuelTest.record: Upper-GI 0-10, lower-GI 0-10, stops, able to drink in last 20 min, temperature. Same pre-run meal and timing each time.
fuelTest.decision: On Jan 3: pick the strategy with the lowest mean (upper + lower) GI score; tie -> simpler/cheaper. It becomes the race fuel for all specific-block long runs, MP sessions, the HM and Rome. If every strategy averages >=3 or GI stops recur, see a sports dietitian/GP (e.g. fructose malabsorption breath test) before raising the carb target further.
fuelTest.caveats: n-of-1 with 2 runs per arm: good enough to spot a clear winner, not to separate small differences. Week 6 follows the LT test and week 11 is Christmas week; note anything unusual eaten the day before.

gates.name: Threshold field test
gates.rule: 30-min TT; replaces device LT {LT:100%} bpm. All threshold and easy-cap HR values in this plan are percentages of LTHR, so updating data/athlete.json with the measured value rescales them.

gates.name: Aerobic check (replaces Dec 20 10K)
gates.rule: HR at 5:30/km vs the Nov 4 baseline (same route, similar temperature), plus the Nov 21 threshold test. Keep progressing to the 88-110 km weeks from Dec 21 if HR at 5:30 is >=3 bpm lower (beyond normal day-to-day noise; Buchheit 2014), weeks 7-9 were completed >=90% and nothing hurts; otherwise repeat the Endurance 5 volume (~86 km) for 2 more weeks before climbing.

gates.name: Pisa Half Marathon (easy, not a checkpoint)
gates.rule: Easy 21 km with sister at ~6:00/km, HR <={LT:85%}. Fuel and cup-drinking rehearsal.

gates.name: 10K checkpoint
gates.rule: <=38:00 2:55 on track (MP 4:09); 38-39 -> re-target sub-3 (MP 4:15-4:16); 39-40 -> re-target 3:00-3:05 (MP ~4:20); >40 -> re-target ~3:08-3:12 (MP ~4:25-4:30). Volume stays as written either way.

principles: Volume modelled on Pfitzinger 18/70: an 18-week block (Nov 9 - Mar 14) peaking at ~110 km, 8 weeks at 85+ km, two medium-long runs a week, long runs up to 34 km, recovery weeks every 3-4 weeks, 3-week taper. Training volume is the training variable most strongly linked to marathon time (Doherty 2020; Tanda 2011).

Injury guard: avoid >30% volume jumps over two weeks (Nielsen 2014). A niggle lasting more than two runs, or resting HR +5 bpm for 3+ days, means repeating the previous week's volume instead of progressing.

Swimming: easy pool sessions replace the Monday recovery run in most weeks (km moved to other easy runs, weekly totals unchanged). Low-impact recovery and extra aerobic time; it does not count as running volume.

Home strength 2x/week (S1 heavy single-leg strength after a quality run, S2 plyometrics + core), 1x in recovery weeks, 1 light session in taper week 2, none in race week (Balsalobre-Fernandez 2016; Blagrove 2018). Equipment: a loaded backpack and a step; adjustable dumbbells or a kettlebell help keep loads heavy.
Easy means easy: HR cap {LT:85%} bpm on every non-quality run until LT1 is measured (Seiler 2010; Stoggl & Sperlich 2014).

Quality as prescribed: continuous LT runs held at HR {LT:95%}-{LT:99%} (ease off past {LT:99.5%}), race-pace work at MP 4:09 (ease to 4:16 if lap HR passes {LT:99.5%}), VO2max reps in race prep. Roughly 80% of running stays easy.
Strength + plyometrics 2x/week in base and specific, 1x in recovery/taper (Balsalobre-Fernandez 2016).
Recovery weeks every 3-4 weeks are not optional, and run volume is not replaced by extra sessions.
Taper: ~2 weeks, volume -40-60%, intensity and frequency kept (Bosquet 2007).

Drink to thirst in long runs and the race; learn sweat rate by weighing before/after long runs; fuel with 1:0.8 glucose:fructose gels/drink mix (no concentrated honey), gut-trained from 40 to 75-90 g/h across the block (Hew-Butler 2015; Goulet 2011; Rowlands 2015; Costa 2017).
Pre-race: low-FODMAP, low-fibre, low-fructose carb load for 24-48 h; no NSAIDs (Lis 2018; van Wijck 2012).
Rome course: ~100 m gain (similar to Munich) but cobbles reportedly km 30-40 and many turns; MP long runs finish on cobbles/turns.
Race pacing: first half no faster than goal MP (Munich: 1:36:24 / 1:43:48 positive split).
